title: External retries preserve completion and idempotency semantics
statement: Every supported retry or duplicate-delivery continuation for a modeled external operation MUST respect its retry policy, completion certainty, idempotency, and required stable identity.
rationale: A response can be lost after an external side effect completes, so treating unknown completion as definite failure can duplicate non-idempotent effects even when every ordinary type and branch is valid.
failure_prevented: Forbidden retries, repeated non-idempotent effects after unknown completion, unstable idempotency keys, or duplicate delivery without modeled idempotent handling or deduplication.
applicability: Environment Contract v1 operations whose supported outcome continuations retry or whose delivery/cardinality admits duplicates. UNKNOWN retry or idempotency remains uncertainty.
evaluation: Fortress compares retrying continuations with NEVER/SAFE/CONDITIONAL/UNKNOWN policy, preserves UNKNOWN_COMPLETION, checks idempotency classes, and proves key identity by exact boundary parameter identity.

finding.message: A modeled retry or duplicate-delivery path violates completion or idempotency semantics.

remediation: Stop the retry, declare and implement truthful idempotency, or preserve one proven stable idempotency/deduplication key across attempts.
valid_example: An idempotent-with-key operation retries after timeout using the same exact boundary key parameter.
invalid_example: A non-idempotent operation retries after UNKNOWN_COMPLETION or duplicate delivery invokes a non-deduplicating handler.
exception_policy: HTTP verbs, function names, and provider conventions do not establish retry safety. Unknown identity remains non-evidence rather than authorization.
history: Introduced with explicit retry, idempotency, completion certainty, and duplicate-delivery semantics.
